---
title: "Case study: a text-analysis pipeline"
---

```{r}
source("_helpers.R")
v <- function(k) val(k)
n_k <- function(k) paste0(round(v(k) / 1000), "k")
```

**When this matters.** As a worked example of the whole method on a real pipeline: what was measured, which rewrites paid, which did not, and what went wrong. The pipeline counted terms and changes across about `r n_k("case_docs")` documents; its main table was about `r v("case_big_gb")` GB in memory, on a laptop with `r v("case_ram_gb")` GB of RAM. Numbers below come from the pipeline author's report`r fn("case_docs")`; they are single measurements on that machine.

## Result

| State | Time | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Before: serial, `memory = "transient"` | `r v("case_before_summed_s")` s summed (about `r v("case_before_wall_min")` min wall) | reference |
| After the changes below, `r v("case_after_nproc")` crew workers, shared memory for the big table | `r v("case_after_wall_s")` s wall, `r v("case_after_summed_s")` s summed | `r v("case_identical_targets")` intermediate targets identical; `r v("case_file_hashes_equal")` of `r v("case_file_hashes_total")` output files byte-identical (the other embeds its save time) |

With workers, wall time approached the slowest dependency chain, which ended in a plot taking `r v("case_slowest_plot_s")` s that could not be sped up without changing the output. `tar_dag.R` reports exactly this bound (critical path).

## Method

1. A profiling subagent with a strict brief: read-only, never `tar_make()`, timings from `tar_meta()`, rewrites benchmarked on subsets loaded with `tar_read()`, scratch scripts outside the repo, findings returned with file:line, measured speedup and risk to output identity. The user picked what to implement.
2. Beyond the slowest targets, it looked for **spread-out costs**: the same expensive function in several targets, and a big object reloaded by many targets (`r v("case_reload_s")` s × `r v("case_reload_n")` loads).
3. Ratios on subsets, then `identical(old, new)` on the full real data before adopting anything.
4. Regression check: snapshot values and file hashes before, compare after (`tar_snapshot.R`). Tracing differences down to rows exposed a real data problem (ligature characters splitting words).

## What worked

| Change | Before → after | Exact? |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed-string prefilter before each dictionary regex (the literal must occur in any match) | `r v("case_prefilter_before_s")` s → `r v("case_prefilter_after_s")` s | yes, by construction |
| Regex only in a window around a rare anchor token | `r v("case_window_before_s")` s → `r v("case_window_after_s")` s, same `r num(v("case_window_matches"))` matches | argued from the pattern; **not exact in general** (see `vectorization.md`) |
| Compute once in a cache target for the union of IDs; consumers look up with `match()` and `stopifnot(!anyNA(i))` | `r n_k("case_cache_before_n")` → `r n_k("case_cache_after_n")` computations; consumers stopped loading the big table | yes |
| Lowercase once, then case-sensitive fixed search | `r v("case_lower_per_term_s")` s per term → `r v("case_lower_once_s")` s once + `r v("case_lower_term_after_s")` s per term (about `r v("case_lower_total_before_s")` s → `r v("case_lower_total_after_s")` s) | ASCII only: a ligature changed a count from `r num(v("case_lower_count_before"))` to `r num(v("case_lower_count_after"))` in a naive version |
| Expensive function on distinct values: `f(u)[match(x, u)]` | `r v("case_unique_before_s")` s → `r v("case_unique_after_s")` s | yes (pure function) |
| `stri_replace_all_charclass()` instead of a regex character class | `r v("case_charclass_before_s")` s → `r v("case_charclass_after_s")` s per 60k texts | yes |
| Crew workers sized by an `NPROC` environment variable; worker deployment, transient memory | one slow plot stopped dominating wall time | yes |
| Shared memory (mori) for the big table across workers, with a custom format (`formats.R`) | fit in memory; no reload per worker | yes, after fixing two traps |
| Dynamic branching over `r v("case_chunks")` stored chunks for the big counting jobs | parallel counting | yes |
| Normalize text to ASCII once, early (fixed table, then transliterate only what remains) | full transliteration `r v("case_ascii_full_s")` s on `r n_k("case_ascii_full_n")` texts → `r v("case_ascii_fast_s")` s for three columns | intended output change; also made the lowercase trick exact |

## What did not work

- Merging all patterns into one alternation regex: slower (`r v("case_alternation_s")` s vs `r v("case_alternation_sep_s")` s) and not identical (overlapping matches).
- A fixed prefilter before each synonym regex, where most texts contain the literal: slower (`r v("case_synonym_prefilter_s")` s vs `r v("case_synonym_plain_s")` s). A case-insensitive fixed search costs more than it saves.
- Speeding up the slowest plot: impossible without changing the output.

## Traps hit

- Returning `mori::share(x)` from a target with an `rds` format and `cue = tar_cue("always")`: the stored value was only a region name, new on every run, so every downstream target rebuilt on every `tar_make()`. Fixed with a custom format that writes real data and re-shares on read (`sharing-mori.md`).
- `dplyr::mutate()` on a shared table keeps the untouched shared columns; saving the result with a plain writer stored only region names and failed in a later session. Fixed by making a copying format the default (`format_qs_unshared`).
- Transliteration side effects: `"µm"` became `"mm"` under a full Latin-ASCII transform; soft hyphens and zero-width spaces must become the empty string `""`, not a space `" "`.
- Mapping branches over a big shared table gives every branch a full copy unless it is shared; chunk it into separate stored targets instead (`branching.md`).

## Lessons that generalize

- Most of the gain came from **doing less work** (prefilters, unique values, computing once, smaller inputs), not from faster functions.
- The cheapest parallel win was making the slowest chain the only thing left on the critical path.
- Every non-trivial rewrite needed a full-data identity check; two "obviously exact" tricks were not.
- Guardrails held throughout: no `tar_make()` in a pipeline with deploy targets without approval, package installs only with approval, every change and its check recorded in the project's decisions log.
